author: feature-implementer
summary: Fixed GET /owners?page=0 rendering the error page. OwnerController.processFindForm clamps the 1-based page request parameter to the first page before translating it to a zero-based PageRequest, which previously threw IllegalArgumentException for any page below 1. Covered by OwnerControllerTests.processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Clamping with Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) removes the attacker-reachable IllegalArgumentException on GET /owners?page=<1 without widening input handling; the parameter stays an int, so non-numeric input is still rejected by binding rather than reaching the repository

No new injection surface: the page value flows only into PageRequest.of and never into a query string; data access remains the Spring Data derived query findByLastNameStartingWith with bound parameters (system-design Threat Model, SQL injection row)
No overflow path introduced: the lower bound is clamped before the page - FIRST_PAGE subtraction, and the upper end only subtracts, so no int wrap is reachable from the request parameter

Output escaping unchanged: currentPage is rendered from a primitive int in owners/ownersList.html, so the Thymeleaf preprocessing expressions on the pagination links cannot carry attacker-controlled text
No error-path information disclosure added: the fix replaces a stack-trace-bearing error page with a normal 200 listing, which reduces rather than increases debug exposure
No secrets, credentials, tokens, or key material anywhere in the diff; no configuration, logging, or serialization surface touched
Supply chain unaffected: the change set is two Java files, with no build.gradle, lockfile, or dependency coordinate changes, so no new CVE exposure is introduced by this pass
Test change is test-only scaffolding (ArgumentCaptor plus AssertJ) with no production reachability

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: FIRST_PAGE constant with javadoc clearly documents the 1-based-vs-0-based page indexing rationale
Math.max clamp is a minimal, readable fix with a why-comment explaining the design choice (malformed input, not failure)
New test processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage follows existing four-phase and parameterized-loop conventions in the file (mirrors processFindFormIgnoresSurroundingWhitespace)
checkFormat and compileJava/compileTestJava both pass clean
No leftover references to the unclamped page parameter after the fix

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The fix guarantees new behavior for REQ-OWN-002's paging bullet (`docs/prd.md:62`, "the matches are listed a page at a time"): a `page` value below one now clamps to the first page instead of erroring (see `OwnerController.processFindForm`, and the new test `processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage`). The PRD's Edge cases list for REQ-OWN-002 does not mention this boundary. The document already has a precedent for recording exactly this kind of boundary/defect behavior inline (edge case 3, the PostgreSQL case-sensitivity defect, and the Known Defects pattern in system-design.md). Without an edge-case bullet, a reader of the PRD alone cannot tell that out-of-range page values are a guaranteed, tested contract rather than an accident of implementation.

approved_aspects: PRD boundary: neither changed file is a docs/ path, so no PRD/system-design mechanism-leak or internal-code-reference risk was introduced.

Cross-document coherence otherwise holds: REQ-OWN-002 already covers OwnerController and paging in system-design.md's Core Contracts table (docs/system-design.md:95), and no anchor, link, or constant reference in the touched files was invalidated.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The test body loops over `List.of("0", "-5")` with a `for` statement to drive two page values through the same MockMvc call and a shared `times(2)` verify. testing-principles.md's Four-Phase Test Structure and Assertions sections both forbid branching/loops in a test body ("No branching in assertions ... no loops"; Agent Decision Checklist item 4, "Linearity"), and this test is newly written (2026-08-05), so the rule applies in full. Convert to a `@ParameterizedTest` with `@CsvSource` (e.g. rows for `0` and `-5`, each asserting `currentPage` is clamped to 1), one case per row, so each page value is an independently meaningful, straight-line assertion instead of a loop.
findings.fix: Replace the `for (String pageBelowOne : List.of("0", "-5"))` loop with `@ParameterizedTest @CsvSource({"0", "-5"})` over a single `mockMvc.perform(...)` call per invocation.

findings.description: Method name `processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage` mirrors the production method name `processFindForm`, which is exactly the anti-pattern testing-principles.md's Test Naming section calls out by counter-example ("`theOwnerSearchShouldMatchOnLastNamePrefix`, not `processFindFormByLastName`"). The naming school (BDD `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`) applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward; this test was added 2026-08-05.
findings.fix: Rename to a behavior-describing name, e.g. `theOwnerSearchShouldClampPageBelowOneToFirstPage`.

approved_aspects: OwnerController.processFindForm correctly clamps page<1 to FIRST_PAGE before translating to the zero-based PageRequest, matching the fix summary in build-pass

New test exercises both a zero and a negative page value, verifies HTTP 200 (not the prior error page), the resolved view, the currentPage model attribute, and the actual zero-based Pageable passed to the repository via ArgumentCaptor -- good behavioral coverage of the clamp
Uses the existing george()/Page<Owner> test vocabulary consistently with the surrounding suite
gradlew test passes with the new test included

author: product-requirements-expert

summary: Owner search lists its matches a page at a time, and a request for a page earlier than the first lists the first page rather than failing. Recorded as edge case 4 of Owner records; the behavior already ships.
acceptance_criteria: given a search whose requested page is earlier than the first page of matches, when the search runs, then the first page of matches is listed and no error page is shown
non_goals: behavior for a page later than the last page of matches, which stays unspecified

Edge cases 1-3 keep their numbers, so existing citations (Open Questions cites edge case 3) still resolve. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log, nothing to judge. No code change is implied by this entry; the shipped behavior already satisfies the criterion.
